The mistake might have occurred when they decided to pivot to C without fully exploring the sources for B. They didn't consistently apply the initial plan of gathering information for B, which was the intended approach.

So, the mistake was made when the agents started focusing on C too early and didn't properly continue with the original plan to validate B as the best answer. This led to a potential oversight in considering the broader impact of the Internet on information access.
